Former Liberal minister Philip Ruddock has been appointed by the Australian cabinet to lead a review. The purpose of this examination is to determine if Australian law provides adequate protection for the human right to religious freedom.

***

The appointment, announced by Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull, is a strategic move to manage a potentially difficult political debate. It is designed to prevent a conflict over religious amendments being added to the pending same-sex marriage bill, which is set to be legislated following a national "yes" vote.

***

However, the review has not settled internal government divisions. Treasurer Scott Morrison stated the review is "no substitute" for immediate amendments. While senior conservatives like Peter Dutton are open to a separate religious freedom bill next year, Morrison and others insist the issue must be addressed at the same time as the marriage bill.

***

Prime Minister Turnbull has emphasized the need for a careful approach, warning against the "high risk of unintended consequences" when legislating basic freedoms. He expressed concern that many recent proposals for religious protections go far beyond the issue of marriage and cautioned against creating uncertainties with vaguely worded, "bill of rights-style" declarations.

***

Mr. Ruddock has been asked to report his findings by March 31st. Turnbull described the review as a "timely expert stocktake" that will inform future legislative reforms. The Prime Minister justified Ruddock's selection by highlighting his experience as Australia's former special envoy for human rights, deeming him the right person for the task.
